messages:
Maria Gonzalez: Heads-up — console alert: validation spike for fncall 'fetch_customer_profile' in prod eu-west started ~1709009900. Seeing ~1.8% of requests hit structured_validation -> REJECT.
Kevin Li: Any obvious payload pattern? logs? :eyes:
Maria Gonzalez: Past 30m sample attached. Most rejects are arrays where we expect object, or `null` for `customer_id`. Example from logs:
```
{"args": ["customer_id", [12345]], "kwargs": {}}
```
(that one returned array in args instead of {"customer_id": 12345})
Julian Park: Weird. Routing change this morning pushed more traffic to the small-variant model (fast-quant) for low-latency slices. That variant's adapter apparently serializes fncall args differently when multi-turn input gets concatenated.
Samir Patel: So customers are getting rejects even though model answered; do we still bill for those? This will upset billing+support.
Maria Gonzalez: Yes, rejects still consume tokens upstream. Ops flagged a billing mismatch ticket. We probably need to avoid charging for strict-validation rejects where fallback exists.
console-bot: Alert summary: 1200 validation_rejects in 1h (peak 45req/min). Top routes: /api/v1/invoke/fetch_customer_profile (72%). Sampling rate: 10% for full payloads.
Kevin Li: Short-term: can we route these calls back to the stable model variant until we fix the adapter? Or soft-validate (log but allow) for that route?
Julian Park: Recommend: 1) soft-validate for route 'fetch_customer_profile' for 2h canary window; 2) add metric validation_reject_rate tagged by model_variant and route; 3) enable 0.5% full-payload capture for rejected requests for postmortem.
Samir Patel: Agree on metrics. For billing: create a temporary attribution rule that excludes REJECTED outputs from token billing for the affected customer segments (or at least for the canary window). Need finance sign-off but we can flag retro credit.
Maria Gonzalez: Also: quick patch to the adapter to coerce single-element arrays to scalar for legacy hooks, and to treat missing customer_id as invalid but not fatal (return a retryable error). I can put a PR up — will need eng-runtime and runtime-adapters review.
Julian Park: If we soft-validate, we should annotate console UX so SRE/product knows why errors drop but customers continue to see answers. Add a dashboard tile: "validation mode" per route (STRICT/PERMISSIVE).
ops-bot: Deployment note: canary routing rollback scheduled if reject_rate > 1% for 30m. Current window: 45m at 1.8%.
Kevin Li: Action items: @Julian to flip routing back (or pin to stable variant) and add metric tags; @Maria to open PR for adapter coercion; @Samir to work billing exclusion; @Product to add console annotation for soft-validate.
Samir Patel: I'll open the billing ticket and ping finance.
Maria Gonzalez: PR posted: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt-adapter/pull/278 — requesting quick review, tests added for array->scalar coercion.
Julian Park: I'll start the temporary soft-validate rollout and add metrics. Dropping routing change if rate not below 0.8% in 30m.
Kevin Li: Thanks. Let's sync in 30m. :thumbsup:
